trajectory.development: Book 24 begins the Long Return's labour. Trained outside-lineage hands set up the labour (E8), a visible shortfall remains (E7), the Book exports a public capability record separate from debt and tally (E10, agent-proposed and truncated in the record), and the date is public so the valley knows how long it has (E11).
trajectory.becomes_available: Trained hands and a known date, so the labour question is met by people now rather than by a schedule (E10, E11).
trajectory.changes: The refusing generation is already asked to give back in this Book (E10), so the finale's answer to who gives has an earlier case to be measured against.

trajectory.development: Book 25 carries the same labour elements as Book 24. Nine element IDs have identical text in both Books (E17), including the steward's accepted gap in the tally (E14) and the visible shortfall (E16).
trajectory.becomes_available: Inferred from E16 and E17: a shortfall that stays visible across two Books is a standing condition, not a one-time event.
trajectory.changes: Inferred: whatever the finale answers must address a labour gap already recorded as persisting, so announcing a giver cannot by itself close it.

trajectory.development: Conditionally: if the trained hands mature into channel labour before the date, the years between Book 24 and the Long Return do work the record does not yet show. Training takes years (E11) and the span is unknown (E13), so no Book number is claimed.
trajectory.becomes_available: Channel labour ready before the date, if training finishes in time. The required span is not recorded.
trajectory.changes: If training is short, the finale's giving must draw on the hands already trained (E8). If it is long, the finale must answer a shortfall that is still open.

trajectory.development: The Long Return pulse arrives, a deep-store surge the architecture places in Book 30 (E1). It needs channel labour before its date and a Gate schedule that routes it, and the choice of channel belongs to the valley (E1). Who gives return labour is still undecided (E2).
trajectory.becomes_available: The finale, where the generation that refused to be counted gives back the water before it is owed (E3), once the mechanism in E2 is chosen.
trajectory.changes: Earlier labour and routing choices become the answer itself. Whether the giving reads as earned depends on whether the routing and the counting were visibly the valley's choices in earlier Books (inferred).

relations.reason: Trained channel labour cannot mature before the date unless training starts in Book 24, so s3 cannot occur without s1.
The pulse needs channel labour before its date (E1), so s4 cannot occur without the labour that s3 may supply.
The public capability record (E10) helps the finale read as chosen, but the pulse does not need it in order to occur.
The labour need in d1 has no settled supplier while d2 is undecided on who gives and who is counted.
Accepting the crew accepts a gap in the tally (E5), which bears on who is counted. No Book 24 or 25 element cites d2 (E17), so this link is inferred.
Book 25 repeats nine Book 24 elements verbatim (E17). The link is sequential only and shows no added dependence.
The finale's who-gives answer can be given by the generation named in E3 only once d2 fixes the mechanism (E2).

culmination.statement: The Long Return is met by the generation that refused to be counted, who give back the water before it is owed.

necessary.text: Channel labour is trained before the public date, since the pulse needs channel labour before it arrives.
A Gate schedule routes the pulse to a channel, and the choice of channel is held by the valley.
The mechanism that decides who gives return labour and who is counted for it is settled. E3 names who gives, but E2 leaves the mechanism undecided.

enrichment.text: Trained outside-lineage hands and the public capability record show who can repair, so the giving rests on recorded capability rather than assigned debt.
The steward's accepted gap in the tally is carried forward, so the giving repays a cost the Books have already shown.

culmination.standalone_value: If the Long Return never arrives, Books 24 and 25 still keep labour begun with people, a visible shortfall, and the steward's accepted gap in her tally as their own experience. The public capability record is agent-proposed and stays a proposal.

alternative_paths.ordering: Defer first labour to Books 27 to 29, after Book 25, so training starts late.
alternative_paths.effect: E11 says labour cannot wait for those Books, and the training span is unknown (E13). The labour may be untrained at the date, and the Book 30 surprise that E6 records as closed could reopen.

alternative_paths.ordering: Route the Long Return surge by Gate schedule alone, without a valley choice of channel.
alternative_paths.effect: The giving would follow the timetable rather than the generation named in E3. The answer to who gives would be carried by the schedule and would read as imposed.

alternative_paths.ordering: Leave d2 unresolved, or choose a third mechanism at the finale.
alternative_paths.effect: The options A, B and C are not defined in the supplied evidence, so none is assessed here. A third mechanism would need to meet the same tally cost the steward accepts (E5).

opportunities.text: The public date (E11) and the valley-held routing choice (E1) together let the valley decide the channel with the labour record in view, so the surge is routed by the people who will give the labour. Neither makes this possible alone.

Inferred: the gap the steward accepts in her tally (E5) and the return asked of the refusing generation (E10) are the same cost seen from two sides, so the finale's giving can repay a gap the Book already shows.

The public capability record (E10) and the known date (E11) let the valley see, before the date, whether enough trained hands exist. A shortfall can then become a visible milestone rather than a surprise at the Long Return (E6).

reader_experience: Readers meet the labour gap first as people, in Book 24: trained hands, a public date, and a shortfall that stays visible. The finale should feel chosen rather than imposed if earlier Books have shown the valley's routing choice and the cost of the accepted gap, and have shown the refusing generation asked to give back before it is owed. Keep the everyday belonging and wonder the author asks for (E4), and do not let the finale read as a debt collected from the uncounted.
open_decisions: Which mechanism (A, B, C or a third) decides who gives return labour and who is counted for it (E2). The options are not in the supplied evidence.
Whether the steward's accepted gap in the tally is closed by the finale or kept as a standing cost.
Whether the public capability record is adopted as a Book 24 element. The record marks it agent-proposed (E10).
Whether the routing of the surge stays a valley choice in scene, as E1 states, or is set by the schedule.
uncertainty: d1 is cited by 18 elements. 12 were excerpted and the listing was truncated (E17). d2 is cited by none in Books 24 and 25.
Book 25 repeats nine Book 24 elements with identical text (E17), so its own contribution is unknown.
The training span and Books 26 to 29 are not in the record (E13). The Book 23 Balance Stones cut (E1) is not supplied as an element.
E10 and E4 are truncated. E6, E7 and E13 are unknown_legacy. E10 is agent-proposed. The capability record's full definition and mechanism options A to C are not visible.
